methods.text: Read the component aloud the way a screen reader would announce it.
Time each state change with a stopwatch and write the number down.
Swap the sample text for a language with longer words and recheck the layout.
Press every control in reverse order and note what breaks.
List what the component shows when data arrives late, partly, or twice.
Look at the screen from arm's length and note what reads first.
Draw the hit area of each control as an outline over the design.
Hand the component to a teammate and stay silent while they try it.
Mark every place a person must wait and give each one a label.
Zoom the browser to 400 percent and fix the first thing that breaks.
Record a short screen capture and step through it frame by frame.
Reload in the middle of every action and check what survives.
Rename each state in plain words a visitor would use.
Measure how far the eye travels from trigger to result, then shorten it.
Use the component with the screen dimmed to its lowest brightness.
Change one property per pass and compare it with the previous pass.

constraints.text: Status text announces each state change to assistive technology.
Hit areas never overlap between neighbouring controls.
Body text keeps a line length under 75 characters.
Text and its background meet a 4.5 to 1 contrast ratio.

tasks.text: Publish button: an action button for a blog editor that checks required fields, shows publishing, and lists what is missing when it cannot publish.
Sync status: a loader for a notes app that shows syncing, synced and offline states and lets someone retry a failed sync.
Change review: a panel for a code review tool that accepts or rejects one block of changed lines and lets someone undo the choice.
Order card: a card for a shop account that shows delivery status and opens the tracking steps for one sample order.
Document upload: an upload area for a document tool that accepts files by drop or browse and lists each file with its size.
Alert settings: a toggle list for an account page that switches each alert type on or off and confirms the saved choice.

temperaments.text: Draws the disputed state on paper before replying.
Asks for the exact number behind every claim.
Rephrases the question until everyone agrees on it.
Waits until the end, then summarizes both sides.
Brings a second example whenever one is challenged.
Sets a time limit on each disagreement.
Splits a large objection into smaller ones.
Writes each agreed point down before moving on.

temperaments: Asks what the user can do with it.
Pushes for one more pass on the weakest state.
Shows a working sample before making a claim.
Checks the small screen before agreeing.
Questions every effect with no useful result.
Asks how a person gets back after a mistake.
Notices uneven spacing before anyone else.
methods: List each state before drawing the first frame.
Build the useful action before adding any motion.
Reserve space for the longest label in every state.
Compare the resting state with the state after an error.
Try every action twice before calling it finished.
Work through the whole control without touching a mouse.
Test with a long name and an empty value.
Make the main action clear before adding a hint.
Remove any effect that hides the result.
Give one transition a clear start, middle and end.
Interrupt each transition halfway and keep the state correct.
Check the edge alignment before adding shadows.
Choose one spacing unit and use it throughout.
Draw focus and pressed states beside the resting state.
Show what changes when the main action succeeds.
Make failure easy to spot and easy to recover from.
constraints: Every action works without a mouse.
Tap targets are at least 44 pixels tall.
Text stays legible at 200 percent zoom.
Every action gives immediate visible feedback.
tasks: Feature details: an accordion for a product page that expands one feature and keeps the other summaries easy to scan.
Preview zoom: a slider for an image editor that changes magnification while keeping the selected area in view.
Save notice: a toast for a project editor that confirms a save and then clears without blocking the work.
Item quantity: a stepper for a shopping cart that changes item count and updates the total.
Product rating: a rating control for a shop that lets someone select a score and change it before saving.
Workspace search: a search field for a team app that filters project names and shows when nothing matches.
